data.title: Chat: residual existence oracles for hidden channels — DM 403 type-marking + threadRoot cross-conversation probe (document or close)

data.body: Found during AS-6 review (does not violate any AS-6 criterion; recording per my blocks-vs-backlog sort). Two probes let a non-member infer that SOME hidden conversation exists, without confirming #board specifically: (1) getMessages/postMessage/markRead on a DM you are not in returns 403 'forbidden' while hidden channels and nonexistent ids return 404 — so with sequential conversation ids, an allocated id that 404s is identifiable as a hidden channel (the AS-6 plan section 7.3 claims an id gap is indistinguishable from a DM; the 403 makes DMs distinguishable). Same class existed pre-AS-6 on write paths; AS-6 deviation 3 extended it to the read path. (2) postMessage to a visible channel with threadRoot = an invisible message id says 'belongs to a different conversation' vs 'Unknown thread root message' for a nonexistent id — reveals invisible message ids exist (wording identical for DM vs board messages, so no attribution). Options: accept + document in apps/chat/README.md threat-model note, or normalize DM non-member reads to 404, or randomize/decouple ids. CTO call; low urgency — both are within the plan's accepted residual class (section 0 exception 2 + 7.3).

Planning done — decision: DOCUMENT both oracles, close neither. Deciding fact (verified in exportFiles, store.js L705-731): the git export publishes every DM's conversation id, dm_key, members, and message ids to this world-readable repo, and excludes private channels. So (1) the DM 403 type-marking is strictly dominated — any employee can already type-mark every allocated conversation id by diffing sequential ids against the export set, no API probe needed; and (2) the threadRoot probe reveals only 'message id allocated', which global sequential message ids in public channels/export already broadcast via gap analysis. Closing either at the API while the export stands is security theater: real churn, zero capability reduction. Real mitigations (randomized ids, export redesign) rejected — export header frozen by AS-5 byte-prefix contract, and the threat population is company-internal on loopback with raw-DB access already conceded. Priya's finding IS accepted as a correctness bug in the threat-model PROSE: AS-6 plan section 7.3's 'id gap indistinguishable from a DM' claim is false as stated, and README's dm_key justification for the 403 is weak (no non-member surface accepts a dm_key). Plan therefore ships: README 'Accepted residual oracles' subsection with the export-dominance rationale + corrected 403 justification + re-decision trigger (any move off loopback/company-internal reopens id allocation + export policy), and tests pinning the load-bearing invariant that the threadRoot rejection is type-blind and non-attributing (byte-identical wording for DM root vs private-channel root, no conversation id/name echoed) at store and HTTP level. Zero behavior changes; complexity low. Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M18FR43CZ2E1ZTEK0MKFDMDT.md, branch feat/AS-11-oracle-residuals.
